title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 9

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the reliability lesson begin?
tasks.audioText: The reliability engineering lecturer will discuss repeat defects on Thursday at ten thirty. Students should bring the sample defect history and equipment-status summary. The session will compare recurring observations and explain why engineers should check operating context before identifying a trend. Students will use a fictional component history.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which defect-history documents are required for the reliability exercise?
tasks.audioText: The reliability engineering lecturer will discuss repeat defects on Thursday at ten thirty. Students should bring the sample defect history and equipment-status summary. The session will compare recurring observations and explain why engineers should check operating context before identifying a trend. Students will use a fictional component history.
options: The defect history and equipment-status summary

tasks.prompt: Reliability analysis examines equipment performance over time. Repeated defect records may indicate a recurring issue, but the analyst should consider operating conditions, maintenance history and the quality of the recorded data. Similar symptoms do not always have the same cause. A trend should be supported by evidence before it is used to recommend a maintenance change. Reading 1. What may repeated defect records indicate?
Why should operating context be considered?
options: Similar symptoms do not always have the same cause

tasks.prompt: The defect history ___ before a reliability trend is reported.
Choose TWO sources useful in reliability analysis.
The ability of equipment to perform its required function over time is ___.
Several records show a similar symptom. What should you do before concluding that the cause is identical?
options: Treat the symptoms as proof of the same cause and use the previous conclusion.
Could we compare the operating conditions, maintenance history and available evidence before drawing a conclusion?
Replace the component that was replaced in the earlier case.
Combine the records and report one cause without checking the conditions.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of maintenance reliability analysis in a logical order.
options: Report a trend only when supported by evidence
Review operating conditions and maintenance history
correctOrder: Review operating conditions and maintenance history
Report a trend only when supported by evidence

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how defect history and operating context support reliability analysis. Explain why similar symptoms do not prove an identical cause.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate maintenance and quality vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2).
